The sensors (usually little metal pieces or at least an indicated spot on the scale for your feet to go) send low voltage electricity through your body, and if your two feet are the two contact points, the shortest distance between the sensors is up one leg and down the other. It measures only the body fat percentage of your legs. For most people, this will be an underestimate of your actual BF %.

If you crouch or bend down, while keeping all your weight on the scale as normal (and trying to keep still), with one foot touching one sensor and a fingertip touching the other, you make the two contact points one of your feet and one of your hands. This will result in a much more accurate reading, as the current travels through a lot more of your total body mass (up your leg, across your torso and down your arm).
LPT: If you have a digital scale that measures bodyfat, touch one foot to one of the sensors and a fingertip to the other sensor for a more accurate, full-body reading.
